questions.q: How does pytest discover which functions are tests?
options: Every function in the project is treated as a test automatically
By naming convention — files named test_*.py and functions named test_*
Tests must be manually registered in a config file before they run
Only functions decorated with @test are discovered
questions.explain: pytest's default discovery is purely filename- and function-name-based, with no registration step.

questions.q: What makes a pytest test pass or fail?
options: Whether the test runs in under one second
Whether the function it calls returns None
Whether its assert statements evaluate to True
Whether the test file has a docstring
questions.explain: assert is the core mechanism: a False assertion fails the test and reports which check failed.

questions.q: Why test a data-validation function's rejection cases (bad input), not just its acceptance case?
options: A function only tested on good input can hide a bug in exactly the failure path real pipelines rely on to catch bad data
There is no real benefit; testing the good case is sufficient
Rejection cases always run faster than acceptance cases
pytest requires at least two test functions per file or it will not run
questions.explain: The whole point of a validator is correctly rejecting bad data, so that path needs its own test too.

options: Automatically retries the code block three times
Asserts that a block of code raises a specific exception, failing the test if it doesn't
Logs the exception to a file instead of raising it
Suppresses any exception raised inside the block
questions.explain: It's used with `with pytest.raises(ExceptionType):` to confirm a function fails the way it's supposed to.

questions.q: Why is a unit test for validate_row() faster and more direct than running the whole pipeline to check it?
options: The whole pipeline cannot be run more than once
It calls the function directly with known input and checks the exact output, without the overhead of running everything else
Unit tests skip the Python interpreter entirely
Running the pipeline always skips validation logic
questions.explain: A unit test isolates just the function under test, which is far faster than exercising the entire pipeline to check one piece of logic.
